basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'Vers. 1. Cumque coepissent homines multiplicari super terram, videntes filii Dei filias'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 1. Cumque coepissent homines multiplicari super terram, videntes filii Dei filias hominum, quod essent pulchrae. Filios Dei appellavit filios Seth qui quandiu se in patris sanctitate incorrupte servaverunt hoc nomine honorari meruerunt, ut filii Dei vocarentur. Sed, postquam carnis voluptate superari conjunxerunt se damnatae stirpi Cain, ejus malitiam imitari coeperunt. Nonnulli filios Dei angelos malignos interpretati voluerunt. Sunt enim quidam daemones improbi mulieribus. Sed melius est, sicut diximus, ut filios Dei filios Seth accipiamus.
